name: auth/passkeys
summary: Add passkey sign-in without replacing the application's existing identity model.
intent: Users can register and use WebAuthn passkeys as a secure authentication method while existing sessions, account ownership rules, and recovery paths continue to work.

rules.text: An authenticated user can register a passkey that is bound to their existing account.
A registered passkey can create a normal application session through WebAuthn authentication.
An account can hold multiple credentials and each credential has a stable server-side identity.
A user can list and revoke their own registered passkeys without affecting unrelated credentials.

invariants.text: Passkey authentication ends in the same session/account model used by the rest of the application.
Registering or using a passkey must not create a duplicate user for an existing account.
Existing recovery and sign-in methods remain available unless the host application explicitly disables them.

security.text: Registration and authentication challenges are single-use, short-lived, and verified server-side.
WebAuthn origin and relying-party identity are validated from trusted server configuration, not request input.
Credential public keys and authenticator metadata needed for replay or clone detection are stored server-side.
Credential listing and revocation enforce account ownership on the server.

acceptance.text: A test or equivalent executable path proves registration options, attestation verification, persistence, and subsequent lookup.
A test or equivalent executable path proves assertion verification creates a session for the credential owner.
A stale, reused, or mismatched challenge is rejected without creating a session or credential.
One account cannot list or revoke another account's passkeys.
